programme: no coherent programme could be named across the twelve factors
role_in_a: not applicable — no shared programme identified across the listed factors
role_in_b: not applicable — no shared programme identified across the listed factors
shared_axis: not applicable — the factors do not converge on a common pathway, complex, or process that would explain co-occurrence in both diseases
reasoning: The twelve factors are drawn from unrelated developmental and physiological lineages — retinal specification (RAX, ATOH7), hypothalamic/pituitary patterning (SIM1, LHX3), hematopoiesis via RUNX partnership (CBFB), motor neuron/pancreas identity (MNX1), hepatic metabolism (HNF4A), hair-follicle/DNA-damage (HR), immune/HLA regulation (HIVEP2), apoptosis (PAWR), and ERBB growth-factor signalling (NRG1) — with no shared complex, pathway, or target overlap connecting more than one or two of them at a time. Where evidence exists it is isolated to single factors (NRG1 with glioma ERBB biology, HHEX and HNF4A with AD GWAS/expression signals) rather than a jointly acting module, so forcing a unifying story would be inventing a mechanism the record does not contain.
support: PMID 34054873 places NRG1 in lower_grade_glioma_and_glioblastoma via neuregulin-family tumour-microenvironment analysis, relevant only to NRG1 alone, not a shared module; PMID 26173052 links an HHEX genotype to diabetes-exacerbated dementia/Alzheimer's risk; PMID 26499758 associates the HHEX/type-2-diabetes GWAS locus with Alzheimer's and Parkinson's risk; PMID 23036584 reports an HHEX/IDE-region epistatic interaction relevant to Alzheimer's disease; PMID 20724036 associates IDE-KIF11-HHEX variants with plasma amyloid-beta; PMID 39604273 reports HNF4A association with hippocampal Alzheimer's disease markers. All six PMIDs support single factors in one disease each and do not establish any cross-factor programme or connect to lower_grade_glioma_and_glioblastoma except for 34054873.
how_to_falsify: Take ChIP-seq or ATAC-seq data from matched Alzheimer's and glioma brain tissue and test whether RAX, ATOH7, SIM1, LHX3, MNX1, HHEX, HNF4A, CBFB, HIVEP2, HR, NRG1, and PAWR show significant co-binding or convergent regulation of a shared target-gene set in either disease; if several of them do converge on common targets or physically interact, the 'incoherent' call is wrong and a real module should be re-derived from that overlap.
caveats: Both diseases share brain tissue, but the 184 patient-group comparisons come from only 3 independent cohort pairs, so the concordance counts are not 184 independent observations. Twelve single-view factors (e.g. L3MBTL1, TOX, CREB5) were excluded for topping only one subgroup, and known tissue-generic regulators (RFX5, HDAC7, EGR4, TAL1, SOX10) were removed before ranking — notably SOX10, the oligodendrocyte-lineage master regulator, is absent because it is generic to brain/glioma tissue, not because it lacks relevance to glioma biology. The Open Targets record shows essentially no direct disease association for any of these factors in glioma, and only HHEX/HNF4A (Alzheimer's) plus NRG1 (glioma) have any literature placement at all.
